(PTI Photo/Shailendra Bhojak) (PTI8_3_2018_000234B) Sardar, who was part of three consecutive Asian Games medal-winning teams, said India were on par with their rivals in ball possession but continued to fall short in man-to-man marking. Gurgaon Former India hockey captain Sardar Singh feels India have the quality to match the best but need greater discipline and sharper man-marking to bridge the gap with European sides and Australia. Sardar, who was part of three consecutive Asian Games medal-winning teams, including the gold-winning side at Incheon 2014, said India were on par with their rivals in ball possession but continued to fall short in man-to-man marking. “We are up there among the best when it comes to ball possession, but what we lack is discipline in man-to-man marking. The tasks given by the coaches, both with and without the ball, are being executed correctly by players 90 per cent of the time,” Sardar told PTI on the sidelines of the Women’s India Open golf. “But there is a big gap in man-to-man marking. You have to play more disciplined hockey to bridge that gap,” he added. He said European teams and Australia were quick to exploit these lapses. “Europeans take advantage in those areas. When we are good individually, why can’t we be strong as a team?” he said. Sardar said Indian hockey had made significant strides over the past decade, with improvements in both the men’s and women’s teams, particularly in physical fitness and mental strength. He urged players to raise their game and make the most of their preparation ahead of major tournaments such as the World Cup. “If we look at the last 10 years, Indian hockey has improved a lot, both in the men’s and women’s sections. We saw this recently in the men’s and women’s World Cups, co-hosted by the Netherlands and Belgium. “Players must realise that they are going to the World Cup, an event that comes only once every four years. They have put in so much preparation at camps. We are mentally stronger and physically fitter than before,” he said. However, Pakistan pushed India hard at the recently concluded Asian Games in Japan, where a last-minute goal secured a thrilling 4-3 win and the gold medal for the Indians. “We don’t care. Pakistan was expected to come but withdrew later for whatever reason. That has nothing to do with us. We have beaten them in the last 15-20 matches, so the decision rests with their federation and the Asian Hockey Federation. Our focus should be on the five teams that are competing and how we can play well against them,” he said. Sardar said India will be overwhelming favourites with the tournament being held in Jalandhar. “Punjab has produced many players for the country, and some of them began their hockey journey in Jalandhar. Now they have the opportunity to play in front of their home crowd. I hope they play good hockey and bring the Asian Champions Trophy home for the country,” he said confidently.
